title: Open-closed recollement
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion with
complementary
open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative
ring. For every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there is a functorial
distinguished triangle

$$
j_!j^{-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow i_*i^{-1}K
\longrightarrow j_!j^{-1}K[1],
$$

where $i_*$ is the (exact) direct image of the closed immersion, and
the first two arrows are respectively the counit and unit of the adjunctions
$j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ on the small etale sites, induced on derived categories by the exact functors. Here $j_!$ is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and direct image is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Functorial means that every morphism $K\to K'$ induces a morphism of these triangles with the three indicated functorial components, including the square involving the connecting map.

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so its direct image on abelian etale sheaves is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. It is also exact on $\Lambda$-module sheaves: the direct-image formula has the same underlying abelian sheaf, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] says that forgetting coefficients preserves kernels and cokernels and is faithful. It therefore reflects exactness: the underlying homology of a sequence is zero only if its module homology is zero (faithfulness reflects a zero identity). Both inverse images are exact on constant-coefficient modules by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Thus all four operations can be applied termwise to complexes and compute their derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]; in particular $Ri_*=i_*$.

proof.text: For a cochain complex $C$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ put $A^r=j_!j^{-1}C^r$ and $B^r=i_*i^{-1}C^r$. In each degree apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], with its module-coefficient clause, to obtain $0\to A^r\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^r}C^r\xrightarrow{\eta^r}B^r\to0$. Naturality of the counit and unit applied to $d_C^r$ gives $d_C^r\varepsilon^r=\varepsilon^{r+1}d_A^r$ and $d_B^r\eta^r=\eta^{r+1}d_C^r$. Thus these are maps of complexes and form a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to A\to C\to B\to0$. This sequence is natural in $C$: a chain map $v:C\to C'$ gives the three maps $j_!j^{-1}v,v,i_*i^{-1}v$, and naturality gives $v^r\varepsilon^r=\varepsilon'{}^r(j_!j^{-1}v)^r$ and $(i_*i^{-1}v)^r\eta^r=\eta'{}^rv^r$ in every degree, giving both commuting squares. No claim about pro-etale sheaves is used.

source.place: Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, applied degreewise; module clause of the cited node

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to this short exact sequence of complexes in the abelian category $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. It gives a distinguished triangle $Q(A)\xrightarrow{Q(\varepsilon)}Q(C)\xrightarrow{Q(\eta)}Q(B)\xrightarrow{\delta_C}Q(A)[1]$. Its naturality clause gives, for every chain map $v:C\to C'$, $Q(j_!j^{-1}v)[1]\circ\delta_C=\delta_{C'}\circ Q(i_*i^{-1}v)$. The first two arrows remain the specified adjunction maps, not merely maps with isomorphic cones.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, including the proof of naturality

proof.text: The preceding naturality identity descends to the derived category. Indeed all the termwise operations preserve quasi-isomorphisms and factor through $Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. For a quasi-isomorphism $s$, both outer maps in the identity of step 3 are invertible; multiplying that identity by their inverses proves the same naturality identity for $Q(s)^{-1}$. Every morphism in the localization is a composite of images of chain maps and such inverses, so the identity holds for every derived morphism and is independent of the representative. In particular quasi-isomorphic representatives give isomorphic triangles with exactly the three prescribed components. The unit and counit descend in the same way; their triangle identities hold termwise, hence after $Q$, and therefore give the induced derived adjunctions. On modules the sheaf adjunctions are [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and the adjunction clause of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] shows that for $K\in D^+$ both outer terms are bounded below with the same lower cohomological bound as $K$. Since $D^+$ is the full triangulated subcategory specified by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the triangle and all its naturality squares lie there. This is the claimed functorial triangle with its counit and unit.
